title: A read-only view's `…` menu in Manage views opens EMPTY (a 180×10px strip), and its tab menu opens on a leading separator
body:
## Symptom

On an object whose every view is code-defined (`src/views/*.view.ts` — no `sys_view` overlay row), so `ObjectView` stamps `readonly: true` on the tab:

1. **Manage views → the row's `…` button opens a menu with nothing in it.** Measured in a real browser: `role="menu"` bounding box `{width: 180, height: 10}`, `innerHTML === ''`. Rendered, that is a thin strip of `bg-popover` straddling the row's bottom border — it reads to a user as a menu that is *clipped or occluded and unclickable*, not as an empty one. Nothing is occluding it; there is nothing in it.
2. **The tab's `▾` menu opens on a leading `role="separator"`** above its single `Manage all views…` entry.

## Cause

Both menus ask a *different question* in the guard than in the entries beneath it.

- `ManageViewsDialog`'s `…` trigger renders on `(onDelete || onDuplicate || onConfigView || onSetDefault)` — whether a **callback is wired**. Every entry under it is *also* gated on `!isReadonly`. The one entry `isReadonly` does not suppress is Duplicate, and the console deliberately wires no `onDuplicate` (#1520). So on a read-only row the guard passes and every entry drops out.
- `ViewTabBar`'s separators state their own condition (`onDeleteView && !isReadonly` opens a fragment that also holds the separator; the manage entry opened one unconditionally) rather than asking "did anything render above me". Its trigger guard has the same shape as the dialog's, so a read-only tab with no `onManageViews` wired opens a fully empty dropdown too.

## Reproduction

`ViewTabBar` / `ManageViewsDialog` with a single `{ readonly: true, isDefault: true }` view and the console's prop set (no `onDuplicate`).

## Not in scope here

Whether a code-defined view *should* be read-only at all is a separate product question (`ObjectView` classifies `isSystem = !saved`), as is `ViewTabBar`'s `allReadonly` rule, which suppresses the per-tab lock badge when *every* view is read-only — on an object with exactly one, code-defined view that removes the only signal explaining why the menu is nearly empty.
